### Step 1 — Scene
This appears to be a breakfast plate: a sausage/meat patty with condiments, a biscuit with white gravy, scrambled eggs, and browned potatoes. The food identities are somewhat uncertain, particularly the upper-left item.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A large, rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:
**Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².**

### Step 3 — Items
Visible foods: meat patty, yellow/red condiments, biscuit, white gravy, scrambled eggs, and browned potato cubes. Cooking fat is included in the energy estimates for the cooked foods rather than added separately.

### Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
The assigned areas sum to **57% of the plate**, leaving about 43% bare. Areas are apportioned between the overlapping foods to avoid counting the same surface twice.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sausage/meat patty | 13% | 69 × 1.6 = 110 ml | 1.0 | 110 g | 300 | 330 kcal |
| Biscuit | 10% | 53 × 1.8 = 95 ml | 0.9 | 86 g | 330 | 284 kcal |
| White gravy | 7% | 37 × 0.65 = 24 ml | 1.0 | 24 g | 100 | 24 kcal |
| Scrambled eggs | 11% | 58 × 1.3 = 76 ml | 0.95 | 72 g | 150 | 108 kcal |
| Browned potatoes | 14% | 74 × 1.8 = 133 ml | 0.6 | 80 g | 180 | 144 kcal |
| Yellow/red condiments | 2% | 11 × 0.6 ≈ 6 ml | 1.0 | 6 g | 100 | 6 kcal |

### Step 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **378 g and approximately 900 kcal**. That weight is plausible for the visible coverage and modest pile heights. Energy is relatively high because the estimate assumes a fatty meat patty and biscuit; different identification of those items would materially change it.
